programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
It’s the last quarter-final of the series, and with a place in knockout week at stake, there’s everything to play for. Four chefs return to the kitchen knowing that one false move could bring their ambitions to an abrupt end. Marcus and Monica are looking for the consistency, ingenuity and confidence that mark out a truly exceptional chef.
First up is the invention test, and the secret ingredient has a history stretching back more than 2,000 years: miso. A staple of Japanese cuisine, this fermented paste brings extraordinary depth, savoury complexity and umami to a dish. With different varieties offering their own distinctive flavours, the chefs must work out how best to make miso the star of the plate. Who will turn this humble ingredient into something exceptional, and who will fall short of expectations?
Then they face one last chance to prove they have what it takes to go all the way.
Three highly respected food writers and critics, Tom Parker Bowles, Leyla Kazim and Jimi Famurewa, wait to put the chefs’ cooking under the microscope. Between them, they’ve eaten at restaurants around the world and very little escapes their attention. They know what exceptional food looks, tastes and feels like, and they’ll be looking beyond technical skill to the details that separate a good meal from a truly memorable one.
The chefs must serve up a two-course menu that captures their culinary identity, showcases their abilities and gives these exacting critics something to talk about. Every choice matters, from the balance of flavours to the smallest finishing touch. Can they cook with enough originality and precision to make a lasting impression?
Back in the kitchen, Marcus and Monica face their biggest decision yet. With the quarter-finals coming to a close and only three places in knockout week up for grabs, they must consider the chefs’ performances across the challenges before deciding who has done enough to progress to the next stage. For those who fall short, there will be no second chance.
Who will take the next step towards the coveted MasterChef: The Professionals title, and whose journey ends at the final hurdle?

Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When a burnt-out delivery van is discovered on a quiet rural road, Rose and Raj are met with a grim crime scene: a charred body in the passenger seat and no sign of the driver. Sifting through the ashes, they uncover a bizarre assortment of clues, including a melted key fob, rusted gardening tools and a bottle of imported Polish vodka.
Tracking down the van’s insured drivers leads them to Kelly Prudham, a tight-lipped agency cleaner, and Scott Smith, a devoted widowed father missing since the previous evening. Is Scott the vanished driver, or is he the unidentified victim in the passenger seat? Kelly claims concern for Scott’s young daughter Chloe, yet she stonewalls every question. However, Rose’s sharp eyes spot an identical bottle of Polish vodka in Kelly’s flat, indicating that Kelly may have a dangerous motive for concealing her and Scott’s recent movements.
Meanwhile, Joe can’t resist probing into the mystery. Dragging Brother Christopher along, he snoops around the crime scene and dives into Scott’s past. Relying on his sharp human intuition and feeling somewhat aligned with this man who seems to be struggling as a father, Joe forms a bold theory about Scott’s whereabouts. But his covert search goes sideways, stranding Joe and Christopher in a perilous predicament deep in the Northumbrian moors.
With time running out and danger escalating, Rose, Joe and Raj must pool their findings to identify the burnt remains, track down the arsonist and expose the motive behind the blaze before the truth burns out completely. programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc:
With exclusive access to the police service on the paradise island of Bermuda, we follow life on the front line for the near 400 officers keeping both holidaymakers and locals safe. From patrols and traffic operations to the drug unit, forensics, tactical response teams, the coastguard and community policing, the series goes behind the scenes with the officers at the heart of the action.
The island has its fair share of challenges on both land and sea, with more than 3,000 crimes committed each year. We show how these dedicated officers, including around 30 from the UK, deal with the highs and lows of policing this British Overseas Territory.
In the centre of the island, Sergeant Milton Hill responds to reports of an elderly man walking along a busy roadside in clear distress. When he arrives, the man is unable to recall his name, address or basic personal details, and the mystery begins. Concerned for his safety, Milton stays close, guiding traffic around him as he repeatedly steps into the road. On an island where everyone knows everyone, Officer Milton sends a photograph of the man to base, where his identity provides a surprising twist to the tale. It's a race against time for Officer Milton to get him returned home safely.
Elsewhere, PC Eddie Smith and PC Jameela Sabir are on a stop-and-search operation. When Sergeant Mervin Homer examines a bike, he discovers a dangerous switchblade hidden under the seat. With the rider offering no feasible explanation, the prohibited weapon is immediately seized. Back at Hamilton Police Station, Custody Sergeant Francis Blackman reads the bike rider their rights, while Assistant Commissioner Martin Weekes examines other recently confiscated blades, including machetes and a samurai sword.
At Bermuda’s international airport, PC Paul 'Geordie' Watson supports Customs Officer Malcolm Martin and drugs dog Zorro while screening an incoming flight from Canada. After sweeping the aircraft cabin in just five minutes, Zorro indicates interest in two bags in the arrivals hall, leaving customs officers the job of discreetly monitoring the family before searching their bags and bringing them in for questioning. What will the canine team uncover next?

Glenn's no stranger to that as he struggles to let go of his feelings for Mack, all while her connection with his replacement Leo blooms. programme.title: Port An Obain
programme.desc:
Baile an Òbain….prìomh bhaile Earra Ghàidheal is Bhòid..cala trang gach latha dhen bhliadhna….le soithichean obrach ..aiseagan beaga, is mòra, uile a’ frithealadh gach duine tha fuireach anns an sgìre. Gu leòr eile tha tighinn a chèilidh air a’ bhaile…air trèana, bus, neo air seòl… tha an t-Òban aithnichte mar aon de na prìomh bhailtean Albannach do luchd-turais….biadh mara sònraichte, agus blas traidiseanta air gach nì eile tha’s a’ tamhainn dha na mìltean a th’ air saor-làithean…..ach se cuideachd àite obrach a th’ ann…. ….muir a’ toirt beò-shlàinte do chuid a tha fuireach anns na h-eileannan eireachdail a tha a’ cuairteachadh na sgìre, ….a dh’aindeoin aimsir neo ràithaichean
Oban is the main town of Argyll and Bute. A busy port 365 days a year, with workboats and ferries of all sizes attending to the needs of the local population. It is increasingly popular with tourists, who arrive by train, bus or under sail - a destination offering exceptional seafood and a traditional holiday experience for the many thousands of visitors to enjoy. But it is also a place of work. The sea provides a living for some who reside on beautiful islands located throughout the Argyll area, and their work continues, despite the weather or the season.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

Tha tè aig a bheil ùidh mhòr ann an surfadh, Ceitlin Lilidh a’ toirt thugainn sreath de dhà phàirt air eachdraidh surfadh air feadh an t-saoghail. Do mhuinntir Tahiti, far an do thòisich surfadh bho thùs, tha e nas motha na spòrs, ’s e taisbeanadh a th’ ann de chultar mhuinntir an uisge, muinntir Pholinìsia.
Le tòrr de chultar agus eachdraidh bheairteach muinntir Pholinìsia cha mhòr air a sguabhadh air falbh, feumar taing a thoirt do leithid Tom Pōhaku Stone oir chaidh traidiseanan a bhith a’ dannsa air bùird fiodha a thoirt chun an ath ghinealaich agus chun an t-saoghail air fad, far a bheil a-nis, na deichean de mhilleanan dhaoine le ùidh ann an surfadh. Airson a’ chiad uair, tha àite aig surfadh aig na Geamannan Oilimpigeach.
Bho bhith na chur-seachad annasach do luchd-turais bhon Taobh an Iar a’ dol a Hawaii tràth anns an fhicheadamh linn gu bhith na phàirt mhòr de dhòigh-beatha na tràghad ann an California air taobh an iar Ameireagaidh. Cha tug e fada gus an do ràinig surfadh cladaichean fuar na h-Alba is dithis no triùir a’ cur aodach snàmh orra agus a’ dol a-mach air na bùird aca fhèin.
Bho stuadhan mòra Tahiti gu dùbhlain nan tonn sa gheamhradh ann an Inbhir Theòrsa agus tachartasan stuadhan mòra Nazaré ann am Portugal. ’S e sgeulachd de spioradalachd, spòrs, daoine ainmeil, fasan agus fealla-dhà a th’ ann an cuairt Ceitlin Lilidh ’s i ag ionnsachadh mu eachdraidh surfadh.
At the 2024 Olympic Games, the world's best surfers competed 20,000km from Paris, in Tahiti. Keen surfer Ceitlin Lilidh presents a series on the world history of surfing. Much more than a sport to the people of Tahiti where surfing was born, it is an expression of a culture, the people of the water, the Polynesians.
While much of the rich culture and history of the Polynesian people was almost wiped out, thanks to guardians like Tom Pōhaku Stone, the traditions of dancing on wooden boards was passed on to future generations and to the rest of the world where it is now practised by tens of millions of enthusiasts. Surfing has now for the first time earned its place at the Olympics.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc:
Tha làn-sgur fuil-mìosa a’ toirt buaidh air an dàrna leth dhen t-saoghal ach, fhathast, tha e duilich dhuinn a bhith bruidhinn mu dheidhinn. Sa phrògram seo, thèid an craoladair, Cathy Nicdhòmhnaill, a choinneachadh ri boireannaich aig gach ìre dhen chuairt aca gus rannsachadh dè dìreach a tha e ciallachadh a bhith dol tro làn-sgur fuil-mìosa san là an-diugh.
A’ comharrachadh Mìos Mothachadh Làn-sgur Fuil-mìosa san Dàmhair, bheir am prògram sùil mionaideach air na tha tachairt ris a’ chorp agus an inntinn aig an àm shònraichte seo agus dè na leigheasan a tha ri làimh gus dèiligeadh ris. Ann an Loch Abair, thèid Cathy a chèilidh air an t-seinneadair is neach-ciùil ainmichte, Màiri Anna NicUalraig, airson còmhradh chàirdeil air a’ bhuaidh a bh’ aig làn-sgur fuil-mìosa orra fhèin agus mar a’ lorg i neart tro bhith bruidhinn a-mach. Ann an Inbhir Nis, coinnichidh Cathy ri dithis dhoctair a tha feuchainn ris an tuilleadh ghoireasan a thabhachd do bhoireannaich air a’ Ghàidhealtachd agus, ann an Glaschu, gheibh i facal air na boireannaich air chùlaibh am buidheann-taic soirbheachail, Menopause Warriors Scotland. Is bidh cothrom aig Cathy fiù’ s feuchainn air beagan yoga a-muigh!
Tro chunntasan pearsanta is fiosrachadh bho sàr-eòlaichean, bheir am prògram seo seachad tuigse air cho dùbhlanach is cho duilich ’s a dh’fhaodas an t-àm seo a bhith ach, cuideachd, na cothroman is an toileachas a dh’fhaodas a bhith na lùib.
Menopause is experienced by half the world and yet it remains a difficult subject to discuss. Broadcaster Cathy Macdonald meets women at different stages of their journey to find out just what it means to go through menopause today.
Marking Menopause Awareness Month, this programme will take a close look at what happens to the body and mind during this transformative time and what treatments are available to help deal with it. In Lochaber, Cathy visits noted singer and musician, Mary Ann Kennedy, for a heartfelt discussion about the impact that menopause had on her life and how she found strength in speaking out.
In Inverness, she meets two doctors hoping to improve provisions for women in the Highlands while, in Glasgow, Cathy spends some time with the women behind the pioneering support group, Menopause Warriors Scotland.

programme.desc:

Bho thug an Ruis ionnsaigh air an Ucràin ann an 2022 tha a’ chrìoch air dùnadh gu tur, ag atharrachadh beatha dhaoine air gach taobh. Anns an Fhionnlainn, cluinnidh Ramsay sgeulachdan bho theaghlaichean a chaidh a’ sgaradh bho an luchd-gràdh air taobh eile na crìche. Coinnichidh e riuthsan air a bheil an dleastanas ‘son tèarainteachd aig a’ chrìoch agus cluinnidh e bho dhaoine a chaill am beòshlaint’ gu h-obann air sgàth an dùnaidh.

Since Russia’s attack on Ukraine in 2022 the border has closed completely, transforming the lives of people on both sides. In Finland, Ramsay hears the stories of families who have been separated from their loved ones on the other side, meets those responsible for securing the border and hears from people who have lost their livelihood overnight because of its closure.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc:
Tha na seòid a’ feuchainn rud a-mach às an àbhaist dhaibh agus a’ dèanamh biadh stèidhichte air lusan. Chan eil sgeul air feòil, iasg no bainne!
Tha Ùisdean a’ tòiseachadh le bhith ag ullachadh Seitan, rud a ghabhar an àite feòil a tha air a dhèanamh à glutan chruithneachd. Tha Ruairidh a’ toirt cruth ùr air biadh a bhios e tric a’ dèanamh aig an taigh ’s e air mothachadh gu bheil an Stiubha Cearc-pheasair Moroccanach aige gu tur stèidhichte air lusan. Tha e a’ dèanamh aran-rèidh sgoinneil bhèagan a thèid còmhla ris. ’S e burgar pònairean a th’ aig Ùisdean mar phrìomh chùrsa, fhad ’s a tha Ruairidh a’ dèanamh rolaichean-isbein bhèagan le pònairean anns an t-sabhs tomàta aige fhèin.
Nuair a tha an Seitan air bruich agus air fuarachadh, tha Ùisdean ga ghearradh an àird agus a’ toirt car air sgiathan circe spìosrach – às aonais na circe. Tha sabhs spìosrach, steigeach ga ghabhail còmhla ris.
The lads venture out of their comfort zone and go plant-based. No meat, no fish, no dairy!
Uisdean starts off by preparing seitan, a meat substitute made from wheat gluten. Ruaridh recreates a recipe he often cooks at home, having realised that his Moroccan chickpea stew is fully plant-based. He accompanies it with an excellent vegan flatbread. A bean burger is Uisdean's main dish, while Ruaridh makes vegan sausage rolls with home-made beans in tomato sauce.
When the seitan has cooked and cooled down, Uisdean slices it up and makes an alternative to spicy chicken wings, without the chicken. The dish is accompanied by a sticky spicy sauce.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Uisdean Macleod Presenter - Roddy Munro Executive Producer - Ishbel Maclennan Production Manager - Mairi Macleod Producer - Kenneth Stewart.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na h-ath cheumannan airson ar misneachadh gus leantainn oirnn a bhith bruidhinn na Gàidhlig. Thairis air an t-sreath seo, bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean co-cheangailte ri gach taobh de ar beatha. Leis gun do dh’ionnsaich i fhèin, bheir Joy dhuinn briathrachas a tha sìmplidh agus furasta a thuigsinn. Bidh stiùireadh ann cuideachd a thaobh a bhith a’ cleachdadh abairtean, le eisimpleirean soilleir tro chòmhraidhean goirid.
Coinnichidh sinn ri luchd-ionnsachaidh èasgaidh, feadhainn a tha ag ionnsachadh as ùr, cuid a bha fileanta ’s a sguir ga cleachdadh agus iadsan a th’ air a bhith ag ionnsachadh fad bhliadhnaichean. Agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh eile dhuinn air Alba is e ann an diofar àiteachan air feadh na dùthcha.Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot agus ann an sreath phodcastan air BBC Sounds.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the next steps to inspire us to speak Gaelic. Throughout the series, she introduces words and phrases on a variety of everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy supports us through pronunciation and vocabulary on topics such as friends, home, work and communication.
We meet diligent learners who have embraced speaking Gaelic, from new learners to lapsed native speakers and the on-off learners who have improved their language skills over the decades. The intrepid Calum Maclean takes us on adventures to hidden treasures around Scotland.
Supporting materials can be found online at www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Executive Producer - Una MacDonald.

programme.title: Duncan Mackenzie - Dileab a' Ghlinne
programme.desc:
’S e stàcair agus eòlaiche eachdraidh-ionadail a th’ ann an Donnchadh MacCoinnich – fear a tha dìoghrasach mu bhith a’ toirt am bàrr eachdraidh a shinnsearan ann an Gleann Inbhir Làthail.
A' leantainn air fiolm shoirbheachail ann an 2022, bidh sinn air sàilean Dhonnchaidh agus an rannsachadh aige a’ gabhail ceum mòr. Air an ùr-lorg, tha clàran sgrìobhte a’ dol air ais gu 1370 a’ toirt sealladh prìseil de bheatha dhùthchail Alba, is tha meud na coimhearsnachd seo – fichead mìle ceàrnagach– a’ daingneachadh a cudromachd.
’S e an t-eòlas gun choimeas a tha aig Donnchadh mu na cnuic is na glinn a tha air ar stiùireadh gu mòr-adhartas is chun na luirg smuaineachail gun fhaoidte gu bheil sluagh air a bhith a’ còmhnaidh an seo bho Linn Ùr na Cloiche, còrr is 5000 bliadhna air ais. Tha na gheibh Donnchadh falaichte air cliathaich beinne aig àird 1600 troigh a’ nochdadh gu bheil e air rudeigin a lorg mu ar sinnsearan tràtha a dh’fhaodadh a bhith cudromach aig ìre eadar-nàiseanta.
Local historian and deerstalker Duncan Mackenzie has a passion for unearthing the history of his ancestors in Inverlael Glen. Following on from a successful film in 2022, we follow Duncan as his investigations take a step forward. Newly unearthed written records stretching back to 1370 give a rare insight into early medieval life in rural Scotland, and the scale of this community - 20 square miles - confirms its importance.
Yet it is Duncan’s unrivalled knowledge of these hills and glens that has led to a major breakthrough and the tantalising discovery that people may have lived here since Neolithic times, over 5,000 years ago. What Duncan finds hidden on the mountainside at 1600 feet suggests he has discovered something about our early ancestors that could be of international importance.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc:
Tha làn-sgur fuil-mìosa a’ toirt buaidh air an dàrna leth dhen t-saoghal ach, fhathast, tha e duilich dhuinn a bhith bruidhinn mu dheidhinn. Sa phrògram seo, thèid an craoladair, Cathy Nicdhòmhnaill, a choinneachadh ri boireannaich aig gach ìre dhen chuairt aca gus rannsachadh dè dìreach a tha e ciallachadh a bhith dol tro làn-sgur fuil-mìosa san là an-diugh.
A’ comharrachadh Mìos Mothachadh Làn-sgur Fuil-mìosa san Dàmhair, bheir am prògram sùil mionaideach air na tha tachairt ris a’ chorp agus an inntinn aig an àm shònraichte seo agus dè na leigheasan a tha ri làimh gus dèiligeadh ris. Ann an Loch Abair, thèid Cathy a chèilidh air an t-seinneadair is neach-ciùil ainmichte, Màiri Anna NicUalraig, airson còmhradh chàirdeil air a’ bhuaidh a bh’ aig làn-sgur fuil-mìosa orra fhèin agus mar a’ lorg i neart tro bhith bruidhinn a-mach. Ann an Inbhir Nis, coinnichidh Cathy ri dithis dhoctair a tha feuchainn ris an tuilleadh ghoireasan a thabhachd do bhoireannaich air a’ Ghàidhealtachd agus, ann an Glaschu, gheibh i facal air na boireannaich air chùlaibh am buidheann-taic soirbheachail, Menopause Warriors Scotland. Is bidh cothrom aig Cathy fiù’ s feuchainn air beagan yoga a-muigh!
Tro chunntasan pearsanta is fiosrachadh bho sàr-eòlaichean, bheir am prògram seo seachad tuigse air cho dùbhlanach is cho duilich ’s a dh’fhaodas an t-àm seo a bhith ach, cuideachd, na cothroman is an toileachas a dh’fhaodas a bhith na lùib.
Menopause is experienced by half the world and yet it remains a difficult subject to discuss. Broadcaster Cathy Macdonald meets women at different stages of their journey to find out just what it means to go through menopause today.
Marking Menopause Awareness Month, this programme will take a close look at what happens to the body and mind during this transformative time and what treatments are available to help deal with it. In Lochaber, Cathy visits noted singer and musician, Mary Ann Kennedy, for a heartfelt discussion about the impact that menopause had on her life and how she found strength in speaking out.
In Inverness, she meets two doctors hoping to improve provisions for women in the Highlands while, in Glasgow, Cathy spends some time with the women behind the pioneering support group, Menopause Warriors Scotland.

programme.title: Greim-Bìdh le Gregor
programme.desc:
Tha Gregor MacLeòid dealasach mu bhiadh ionadail. Bho dhachaigh ann an Eilean Leòdhais, tha e a’ sealltainn dhuinn na daoine agus na h-àiteachan gum bi e a’ dol airson a’ bhìdh as fheàrr.
Air taobh sear an eilein, tha e a’ coinneachadh ri iasgair às an eilean gus na muasgain-caola as ùire fhaighinn airson paella mòr dathach. Seo dreach eileanach air fèist às na Meadhan-thìrean.
Tha e cuideachd a’ dol gu bothan beag taobh an rathaid gus silidh sùbhaig a chaidh a dhèanamh aig an taigh fhaighinn. Tha e a’ cleachdadh seo ann an reasabaidh a bheir fìor chofhurtachd do dhuine sam bith – roly-poly silidh.
Do Ghregor, chan eil càil nas fheàrr na càise. Tha e a’ còrdadh ris a bhith a’ dèanamh oidhirp a bharrachd nuair a thig e gu bhith ag ullachadh clàr le càise. Tha e ag innse mun reasabaidh aige airson briosgaidean measan is cnothan, airson a ghabhail cuide ri taghadh dhen chàise as fheàrr leis.
Gregor MacLeod is passionate about local produce. From his home on the Isle of Lewis, he shows us the people and places that provide the finest ingredients.
On the island’s east coast, he meets a local fisherman to pick up the freshest langoustines for an enormous, vibrant paella. This is Hebridean-style feasting inspired by the Mediterranean. He also visits a local honesty shed to pick up home-made raspberry jam to use in the most comforting way – jam roly-poly.
Gregor likes to go the extra mile when preparing a cheeseboard. He shares his recipe for fruit and nut crackers to have alongside a selection of his favourite cheeses.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Gregor Macleod Director - Ramsay MacMahon.

programme.title: Am Balla (The Wall)
programme.desc:
Leth-cheud bliadhna às deidh deireadh Cogadh, tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ dol air turas gus faighinn a-mach mar a tha an cogadh agus sgaradh na dùthcha fhathast a’ toirt buaidh air daoine ann am Bhietnam an-diugh. Tro thuras, chì Ramsay seann shaighdearan bhon dà thaobh a tha a’ tighinn aghaidh ri aghaidh airson a’ chiad uair bho thàinig an cogadh gu crìoch. Thèid e a-mach còmhla ri sgiobaidhean a tha ag obair gus bomaichean is mèinnean nach deach an spreadhadh a thoirt às an talamh; agus cluinnidh e sgeulachdan mu dhaoine a tha fhathast beò le buaidh cogadh le stuthan ceimigeach.
Half a century after the end of the Vietnam War and the country's reunification, Ramsay MacMahon embarks on a journey to discover how war and division continue to affect people in Vietnam today. During his journey, Ramsay meets former soldiers from both sides who come face to face with each other for the first time since the war ended. He joins teams working to clear unexploded ordnance from the ground; and he hears the stories of people still living with the consequences of chemical warfare.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

Mu dheireadh thall, tha a triùir leanabain aig Kinga na gàirdeanan, fhad ’s a tha Emily a’ dol tro dheuchainnean a bharrachd. Tha fradharc Diane ann an cunnart, gheibh Treasa agus Ian naidheachd a dh’fhàgas an cridheachan briste, agus tha Tom Òg a’ ruighinn clach-mhìle chudromach.
Kinga finally holds her triplets together, while Emily undergoes further tests. Diane faces a risk to her sight, Treasa and Ian receive devastating news, and Tom Óg reaches a key milestone.

In Gaelic with English subtitles.

Tha a’ choimhearsnachd a’ cruinneachadh aig cèilidh gus airgead a thogail do Mhàiri, a tha fhathast a’ faighinn seachad air an tubaist aice ‘sa mhuileann. Tha smùid air Boyd ‘s e a’ cur aghaidh air Mairead ‘s Cairistiona air beulaibh a h-uile duine aig a’ chèilidh. Tha cùisean a’ dol ceàrr eadar Johan is Murdina, a’ fàgail gu bheil teine a’ tòiseachadh anns an taigh-òsta – le Murdina agus Boyd glaiste na bhroinn. Am faigh iad às beò?

Hilda - Mischa Macpherson Flòraidh (Frida) - Lauren Macdonald Daibhidh (David) - Ellen MacDonald Mum - Anna Murray Executive Producer - Bill MacLeod Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc:
Tha na seòid a’ feuchainn rud a-mach às an àbhaist dhaibh agus a’ dèanamh biadh stèidhichte air lusan. Chan eil sgeul air feòil, iasg no bainne!
Tha Ùisdean a’ tòiseachadh le bhith ag ullachadh Seitan, rud a ghabhar an àite feòil a tha air a dhèanamh à glutan chruithneachd. Tha Ruairidh a’ toirt cruth ùr air biadh a bhios e tric a’ dèanamh aig an taigh ’s e air mothachadh gu bheil an Stiubha Cearc-pheasair Moroccanach aige gu tur stèidhichte air lusan. Tha e a’ dèanamh aran-rèidh sgoinneil bhèagan a thèid còmhla ris. ’S e burgar pònairean a th’ aig Ùisdean mar phrìomh chùrsa, fhad ’s a tha Ruairidh a’ dèanamh rolaichean-isbein bhèagan le pònairean anns an t-sabhs tomàta aige fhèin.
Nuair a tha an Seitan air bruich agus air fuarachadh, tha Ùisdean ga ghearradh an àird agus a’ toirt car air sgiathan circe spìosrach – às aonais na circe. Tha sabhs spìosrach, steigeach ga ghabhail còmhla ris.
The lads venture out of their comfort zone and go plant-based. No meat, no fish, no dairy!
Uisdean starts off by preparing seitan, a meat substitute made from wheat gluten. Ruaridh recreates a recipe he often cooks at home, having realised that his Moroccan chickpea stew is fully plant-based. He accompanies it with an excellent vegan flatbread. A bean burger is Uisdean's main dish, while Ruaridh makes vegan sausage rolls with home-made beans in tomato sauce.
When the seitan has cooked and cooled down, Uisdean slices it up and makes an alternative to spicy chicken wings, without the chicken. The dish is accompanied by a sticky spicy sauce.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Uisdean Macleod Presenter - Roddy Munro Executive Producer - Ishbel Maclennan Production Manager - Mairi Macleod Producer - Kenneth Stewart.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop a’ leantainn oirre ’s i gar toirt tro cheumannan a bharrachd ann a bhith ag ionnsachadh na Gàidhlig. Bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean làitheil agus, mar thè a dh’ionnsaich na Gàidhlig i fhèin, bheir Joy mìneachadh dhuinn air briathrachas, gràmar is gnathasan-cainnte ann an dòigh a tha furasta a thuigsinn.
Coinnichidh sinn ri luchd-labhairt èasgaidh a th’ air Gàidhlig ionnsachadh gu àrd ìre neo a thogadh leis a’ Ghàidhlig air falbh bho sgìrean traidiseanta na Gàidhealtachd, agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh dhuinn air annasan is cuspairean ’s e air chuairt air feadh na dùthcha.
Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot, ann am pod-chraolaidhean SpeakGaelic air BBC Sounds agus tha na prògraman air fad rin lorg le fo-thiotalan air sianal YouTube SpeakGaelic.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the next steps to inspire us to keep on speaking Gaelic. As in previous series, she introduces and explains usage for words and phrases on everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy will support us through vocabulary, grammar and idiom on topics such as medicine, politics, community and exercise.
We meet diligent speakers who have embraced the language, and the intrepid Calum Maclean ventures to forgotten corners of Scotland seeking hidden treasures.
Supporting materials can be found online: www.speakgaelic.scot, in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds and with English subtitles on SpeakGaelic’s YouTube channel. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Presenter - Calum Maclean Producer - Donald Macleod Executive Producer - Una McDonald.

Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Port An Obain
programme.desc:
In the village of Appin, Gregor MacCormick shows his collection of vintage engines, and retired sea captain Eric Smith visits the new lighthouse ship, the Pole Star.
Ann a baile Appain tha Gregor MacCormaig a sealltainn na seann einseanean. Agus anns an Obain tha Captein Eric Mac’a Ghobhainn a ceilidh air am Pole Star ura.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ro Thrath don t-Saoghal/Born too Soon
programme.desc:
Tha Daisy a’ faighinn leigheas èiginneach agus i a’ strì ri a h-anail a tharraing, fhad ’s a tha Treasa agus Ian a’ cur fàilte air na leth-aoin aca agus gan ullachadh fhèin airson Joshua a chall. Tha piseach a’ tighinn air Diane, agus thèid Méabh a ghluasad nas fhaisge air a dachaigh.
Daisy receives emergency treatment for severe breathing problems, while Treasa and Ian welcome their twins and prepare to lose Joshua. Diane makes progress, and Méabh is transferred closer to home.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc:
Is docha nach eil Zac cho òg is a bha e ach chan eil sin ag radh gum bu choir dha a sguir a bhruadar. Tha a chridhe a seinn , ach an can duine gur e ceòl a th'air a bhilean?
Zac has never settled into normal, responsible adult life, and he wants one more chance at pop stardom. When opportunity knocks, he opens the door and grabs it with both hands, making sure no strings are left unpulled.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc:
Tha Bagelean Abigail fìor bhlast' agus sònraicht' 'son bruinse no lòn, no fiù 's aig àm sam bith, 's 'ad gad shàsachadh ann an dòigh nach gabh inns' 's iad fèìr taght' 'son an roinn leis an teaghlach no le caraidean.
Abigail’s bagels are a very special and tasty brunch or lunch, or anytime experience, satisfying to the extreme and just the thing to share with family and friends.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Glan Fhèin
programme.desc:
Angela clashes with angry locals shouting about short-term lets. Betty and Dido de-escalate things and share some home truths. There’s a sticky situation when an activist called Adam sneaks through the catflap with a tube of superglue.
Meanwhile, Daniel tests Katie’s management methods by renegotiating his contract. And a corporate relaunch that is definitely not a party features costumes, cocktails, new clients and wild dance moves. Ultimately the rivals seem to be getting closer than ever. Katie - Hannah McKirdy Angela - Lana Pheutan Seonaidh - Iain Beggs Dido - Mairead Hamilton Daniel - Calum Macdonald Director - Fiann Macleod Producer - Marie McDonald Writer - Hannah McKirdy Writer - Lana Pheutan.

programme.title: An t-Uisge/Rain Stories
programme.sub-title: Beo Leis An Uisge/Living with Rain ║ Ant-Uisge/RainStoriesS1E2/3
programme.desc:
Tha Anne Lundon a’ lìbhrigeadh an t-sreath ùr, fiosrachail seo a’ rannsachadh an t-saidheans agus na sgeulachdan air cùlaibh an nì a tha a’ beathachadh dhaoine – ’s e sin an t-uisge.
Anns a’ phrògram seo, bidh sinn a’ faighinn a-mach mu mar a tha uisge a’ toirt buaidh air cultaran air feadh an t-saoghail agus air luchd-ealain, a’ leigeil le coimhearsnachdan fàs.
Bidh Anne a’ tadhal air aon de na taighean-staile as ùire ann an Alba airson ionnsachadh mun cheangal a th’ eadar uisge agus an deoch nàiseanta againn. Agus tha i a’ cumail oirre timcheall na h-Emirates Arabach Aonaichte, dùthaich san fhàsach, a tha ag ùrnaigh airson uisge gu cunbhalach agus gu poblach air an telebhisean.
Ach ’s ann ann an Assam sna h-Innseachan a tha sinn a’ lorg an traidisean as dathtiche ceangailte ri uisge. Tha coimhearsnachd a’ tighinn ri chèile gus an t-uisge a thàladh le bhith a’ cumail banais chosgail eadar dà losgann.
Anne Lundon presents this revealing series exploring the science and stories behind the life-giving force that is rain. In this episode, we discover how rain affects cultures around the world, influencing artists and allowing societies to flourish.
Anne visits one of Scotland’s newest island distilleries to find out the connection between rainwater and our national drink. And she continues her journey around the United Arab Emirates, a desert country which holds regular televised public prayer for rain.
But it’s in Assam, India, where we find the most eye-catching rain tradition. A community comes together to summon the rains by holding a lavish wedding - for two frogs.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Anne Lundon Series Producer - Huw Maredudd Director - David Martin.

programme.sub-title: An Dìnnear Mhòr aig Bernie ║ CreagnamButhaidean/PuffinRockS2E12/39

programme.title: Tannadice '87
programme.desc:
Tha 2017 a' comharrachadh an 30mh ceann-bliadhna bho rinn Dundee United FC rud a bha mòran dhaoine a' smaointinn a bha do-dheànta dhaibh: faighinn gu cuairt dheireannach Cupa UEFA. Tha Tannadice87 ag innse sgeulachd iongantach an iomairt Eòrpaich sin, bliadhna san do theab Dundè, a tha ainmeil airson silidh, diut agus naidheachdas, clach eile a chur air càrn urraim a' bhaile.
2017 marks the 30th anniversary of the year that Dundee United FC delivered on what many believed to be an impossible goal; reaching the final of the UEFA Cup. Tannadice '87 tells the remarkable story of this European adventure, a year in which dreams became reality, and Dundee, a city with a reputation for jam, jute and journalism added a fourth 'j' to its trademark: jubilation. Presenter - Alex O'Henley Executive Producer - Ishbel Maclennan Producer - Margot McCuaig.

programme.title: An Cruinne Caochlaideach/Dynamic Planet
programme.desc:
Tha deigh aig pòlaichean a’ phlanaid agus mullaichean nam beanntan ag atharrachadh gu mòr. Thèid tòrr dheth à sealladh san linn seo. Tha na cruthan-tìre deighe seo a’ dol tro chruth atharrachadh, ach tha buaidh aig an leaghadh a’ dol nas fhaide buileach – chan eil àite sam bith sàbhailte bho na dh’ fhaodadh tachairt.
Fhad ’s a tha uisge reòthte a’ leaghadh bho na h-eigh-shruthan, siotaichean deighe pòlarach agus deigh na mara, tha e ag atharrachadh patarain aimsire agus sruthan mara, agus chan eil an saoghal mar a tha sinne eòlach air cho aithnichte dhuinn.
A’ falbh air turas iongantach bho phòlaichean reòthte an Antartaig agus an Artaig gu àrd-chlàran mòr agus sgurran na Himalayas, tha sgioba sònraichte de eòlaichean a’ tabhainn adhbhar dòchais airson àm ri teachd as aonais deighe. Tha sinn a’ sreap am broinn eigh-shruthan, a’ tighinn faisg air ròin, mucan-mara dhronnach agus mathain bàna gus tuigse fhaighinn air mar a tha beatha agus nàdar ag atharrachadh agus a’ glacadh modhan bheathaichean, nach deach fhaicinn a-riamh, air film.
Tha am prògram seo a’ taisbeanadh mar a tha nàdar a’ lorg dòigh, agus mar a tha saidheans agus traidisean gar ullachadh fhèin agus ar Cruinne Caochlaideach airson àm ri teachd a tha ag atharrachadh aig astar.
Ice at the planet’s poles and mountain peaks is changing drastically. Much will disappear completely this century. These icescapes are transforming, but the impact of the melt goes much further - nowhere on the planet is immune from the sometimes-unexpected consequences. As frozen water melts from glaciers, polar ice caps and sea ice, it changes weather patterns and ocean currents, and the world as we know it.
Journeying from the frozen poles of Antarctica and the Arctic to the vast plateaus and soaring peaks of the Himalayas, an extraordinary team of experts offer hope for a future with less ice.
We climb into glaciers and capture never seen before animal behaviour on film - getting up close with seals, humpback whales and polar bears to understand how life is changing and nature is adapting. This programme reveals how nature finds a way, and how science, and tradition can help prepare us and our Dynamic Planet for a fast-changing future.

programme.desc:

programme.title: Celebration Kitchen
programme.desc:
Matt Tebbutt hosts this special edition celebrating Guru Nanak Gurpurab or the Birthday of Guru Nanak, the founder of the Sikh faith. Considered one of the most important Sikh holy days, it is a revered celebration in Sikhism which brings people together in devotion, reflection and unity.
Every year, the occasion is marked on the full moon day of the Kartik month, which is also known as Kartik Purnima, and falls on Tuesday 24 November this year. Three exceptional cooks join Matt in the studio to share their delicious recipes that are perfect for the celebration. Award-winning British Indian food writer, columnist and trend consultant Gurdeep Loyal prepares extra-crispy potato and chickpea tikkis with a tamarind and date chutney, which would traditionally be served as street food outside the temple. Food writer, restaurateur and chef-owner of Jikoni, Ravinder Bhogal, prepares a decadent, celebratory vegetarian platter, and as no feast is complete without a sweet treat, Manpreet Singh Ahuja, aka the Singing Chef, serves up a trio of delicious sweets, including the pinnis that he remembers his mother and grandmother making for Guru Nanak Ji's birthday.
Celebrity guests include doctor and BAFTA award-winning TV presenter Dr Ranj Singh, journalist, broadcaster and best-selling author Sathnam Sanghera and journalist, broadcaster and Good Morning Britain host Ranvir Singh, who shares her cherished Guru Nanak Gurpurab traditions, memories and food favourites from the celebration. The programme also features highlights from the BBC archives. It is a show filled with fun, food and fascinating insights into one of the most important days in the Sikh calendar. programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The oceans have seasons just as the land does. Stretching across the temperate bands located between the freezing poles and the warm tropics lie the seasonal seas. Life is tough in these constantly changing waters, but if animals can persevere and adapt to change, there are myriad opportunities to not only survive but thrive here.
Winter in the seasonal seas is a battlefield. Storms whip up immense waves that can travel for thousands of miles, building to 30 metres in height before making landfall. On the Pacific coast of South America, such waves impact the lives of South America sea lions that have lived on this exposed coast for generations. Newborn pups and mothers are restricted to the colony, but the most intrepid males take a risk, leaving the tempestuous coast for unfamiliar waters and unusual prey - black-necked swans.
Some choose to escape, whilst others are undeterred by winters icy grip on the seasonal seas. In Patagonia, a female southern right whale arrives in the protected bay where she was likely born, in search of a mate. Testing prospective partners before accepting the best mate, she is rewarded with a gentle belly rub and embrace - a valuable pairing given that these animals were hunted to near extinction in the last century. The whaling ban increased this population from just 300 to 25,000, with a surprising twist – white calves.
As daylight lengthens and spring approaches, the greening of the seasonal seas commences. Plankton multiplies, creating huge blooms and feeding many species, including a rather peculiar crustacean, a porcelain crab. In the waters off Chile, over 200 million feast on this bounty, forming the largest-known aggregation of crabs in our oceans. But with limited space and an increased flow of plankton, the crabs do something remarkable - they organise themselves into structured lines, a behaviour that has never been filmed before.
As forests flourish on land, they also do so in the water. In spring, kelp, one of the fastest-growing organisms on earth, can lengthen by half a metre a day, forming submarine jungles that are home to a variety of creatures. In Japan, these lush fronds conceal a rarely seen fish, an eelpout, with a length of just ten centimetres.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
In the frozen waters of the Arctic, a bowhead whale breaks the sea ice with its skull to breathe - completely at home in this seemingly hostile sea. Polar waters may seem remote, but their influence supports more than the wildlife that thrives there by helping to power a global system of ocean currents that creates extraordinary opportunities for wildlife far beyond the ice.
In the Falkland Islands, nutrient-rich water flowing north from Antarctica sustains a colony of king penguins. But returning parents weighed down with food for their chicks must try to cross a beach patrolled by an extraordinary southern sea lion, the only one known to regularly hunt king penguins on land.
Cold water from the Arctic also travels thousands of miles. In the Pacific, it cools the coast of Japan, where a male dwarf lumpsucker, about the size of a pea, must find a nest and persuade a female to enter. Once she has laid her eggs, he becomes a devoted single father, guarding them from hungry predators for 40 days and nights.
Around Antarctica, hundreds of fin whales converge on one of the greatest feeding grounds on earth. They work together in a spectacular synchronised formation, turning clockwise before lunging onto their sides to feast on Antarctic krill. Beneath the continent’s sea ice lies a remarkable world where giant sea spiders clamber over ancient glass sponges and a tiny amphipod escapes hungry icefish by hitching a ride on sea angels and venomous jellyfish.
The influence of the polar waters is so strong that it helps power global currents that cross entire oceans and circle the planet. In the North Atlantic, the Gulf Stream brings warm water from the Caribbean to the shores of Britain, attracting Atlantic bluefin tuna to hunt off the Cornish coast. These powerful predators, which can attack at 45 miles per hour, have only recently returned to British shores following international action to protect them.
But the currents all these animals rely on are changing. With a loss of sea ice, many are now weakening, driving animals to adapt – sometimes in surprising ways. Around Newfoundland, green sea urchins are losing the kelp forests that once protected them from the sun’s ultraviolet rays.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
The final week of heats continues as another group of ambitious professional chefs steps up to prove they have the talent and technique to progress in the competition. But before they can look ahead, they must navigate two demanding challenges that will put their culinary skills and composure to the test.
First, it’s the skills test, where the chefs must fillet a sea bream and use it to create a shellfish risotto, finished with a spinach garnish. It’s a deceptively demanding dish, requiring sharp filleting skills to prepare the fish cleanly, precise timing to achieve perfectly cooked rice and the finesse to build a rich, balanced risotto without losing the delicate flavours of the seafood. Every element must come together seamlessly, with no room to hide behind elaborate presentation.
For some, the combination of intricate preparation and exacting technique proves daunting, leaving them struggling to keep pace. Others take the challenge in their stride, showing the confidence and control of seasoned professionals. Will the chefs’ efforts impress the judges, or will their shortcomings leave Marcus and Monica questioning whether they have what it takes to make it to the next stage?
With the skills test behind them, the chefs have the chance to show Marcus and Monica what they can do when given the freedom to cook their own food. In the signature dish round, they have 90 minutes to create a plate that reflects their personality, showcases their strengths and makes a compelling case for why they deserve to progress.
For some, it’s an opportunity to demonstrate real ambition and push their cooking in exciting new directions. For others, finding the right balance between ambition and execution proves more difficult.
The judges must decide whose cooking has made a strong enough impression to keep them in the running and whose journey ends here. programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.sub-title: Glasgow - A Fix at the Top of the Cathedral ║ S1
programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Dom and Lucia are in Scotland’s biggest city for one of their biggest, or at least highest, fixes yet. Roof works mean once-in-a-generation access to Glasgow Cathedral’s weathervane, so the pair are helping blacksmith Stacey and apprentice Jameel clean and re-gild this iconic cockerel. The medieval building has a storied history, but it definitely predates lifts, so Lucia volunteers to go boldly where no Repair Shop expert has gone before – straight to the top of the 225-foot-high spire.
Back on solid ground, Kaming, a member of Glasgow’s Hakka Chinese community, has a Chinese unicorn head he hopes Lucia can bring back to life. The fragile bamboo-and-paper mask plays an important part in celebrations and festivities, but years of vigorous dancing have left it tattered and torn, its once-proud horn now held on with sticky tape. As he is the last person, as far as he is aware, who still knows how to do the traditional dance associated with the mask, he hopes having the costume repaired will mean he’s able to teach it to future generations before it's lost forever. It’s not a simple fix though, as Lucia has to contend with unfamiliar materials and balance her artistic restoration with creating a mask that will stand up structurally to years' more use in the future.
As they travel the country, the Repair Shop experts love to meet fellow craftspeople, but it’s not all stonemasonry and pottery. There’s been a vibrant graffiti scene in Glasgow for decades, and Dom is meeting celebrated street artist Pizzaboy to discover how his large-scale works engage with the local community. programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
Five chefs remain in the race for a spot in the quarter-final, but first they must impress in two more challenges designed to test their creativity, precision and technical ability.
Marcus and Monica are joined by acclaimed South African chef Ash Valenzuela-Heeger, winner of the prestigious 2025 Michelin Young Chef Award. Her impressive career has seen her hone her craft at some of the world’s most celebrated restaurants, including London’s three-Michelin-starred Ledbury and Cape Town’s renowned Test Kitchen. She has since made her mark with Riverine Rabbit in Birmingham, which earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025.
Known for her bold, inventive cooking, Ash draws on her South African heritage and international influences, with live-fire techniques at the heart of her culinary style. She challenges the chefs to cook BBQ beef sirloin, served with BBQ maitake mushrooms, caramelised roscoff onions and a cafe au lait sauce. It’s a brief that demands a sophisticated understanding of flavour, smoke and fire, and the ability to make every element work in harmony.
With the standard rising and a quarter-final place within reach, can the contestants deliver a plate worthy of this award-winning chef’s exacting standards?
The signature dessert round is the final hurdle, and the chefs must show that they have the range and imagination to compete with the very best. This is their chance to take risks, bring their own ideas to the plate and prove that they can deliver something truly memorable. But sweet cooking demands a different kind of judgement; flavours must work in harmony, textures need to complement one another, and the finishing touches can make all the difference between a good dessert and a great one.
Marcus and Monica have seen what the chefs can do with savoury ingredients, but now they must decide who has the finesse and creative flair to progress to the next stage of the competition. As the final plates are tasted, will the desserts be enough to secure a place in the quarter-final? And whose MasterChef journey must come to an end? programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
It’s the last quarter-final of the series, and with a place in knockout week at stake, there’s everything to play for. Four chefs return to the kitchen knowing that one false move could bring their ambitions to an abrupt end. Marcus and Monica are looking for the consistency, ingenuity and confidence that mark out a truly exceptional chef.
First up is the invention test, and the secret ingredient has a history stretching back more than 2,000 years: miso. A staple of Japanese cuisine, this fermented paste brings extraordinary depth, savoury complexity and umami to a dish. With different varieties offering their own distinctive flavours, the chefs must work out how best to make miso the star of the plate. Who will turn this humble ingredient into something exceptional, and who will fall short of expectations?
Then they face one last chance to prove they have what it takes to go all the way.
Three highly respected food writers and critics, Tom Parker Bowles, Leyla Kazim and Jimi Famurewa, wait to put the chefs’ cooking under the microscope. Between them, they’ve eaten at restaurants around the world and very little escapes their attention. They know what exceptional food looks, tastes and feels like, and they’ll be looking beyond technical skill to the details that separate a good meal from a truly memorable one.
The chefs must serve up a two-course menu that captures their culinary identity, showcases their abilities and gives these exacting critics something to talk about. Every choice matters, from the balance of flavours to the smallest finishing touch. Can they cook with enough originality and precision to make a lasting impression?
Back in the kitchen, Marcus and Monica face their biggest decision yet. With the quarter-finals coming to a close and only three places in knockout week up for grabs, they must consider the chefs’ performances across the challenges before deciding who has done enough to progress to the next stage. For those who fall short, there will be no second chance.
Who will take the next step towards the coveted MasterChef: The Professionals title, and whose journey ends at the final hurdle?

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When a burnt-out delivery van is discovered on a quiet rural road, Rose and Raj are met with a grim crime scene: a charred body in the passenger seat and no sign of the driver. Sifting through the ashes, they uncover a bizarre assortment of clues, including a melted key fob, rusted gardening tools and a bottle of imported Polish vodka.
Tracking down the van’s insured drivers leads them to Kelly Prudham, a tight-lipped agency cleaner, and Scott Smith, a devoted widowed father missing since the previous evening. Is Scott the vanished driver, or is he the unidentified victim in the passenger seat? Kelly claims concern for Scott’s young daughter Chloe, yet she stonewalls every question. However, Rose’s sharp eyes spot an identical bottle of Polish vodka in Kelly’s flat, indicating that Kelly may have a dangerous motive for concealing her and Scott’s recent movements.
Meanwhile, Joe can’t resist probing into the mystery. Dragging Brother Christopher along, he snoops around the crime scene and dives into Scott’s past. Relying on his sharp human intuition and feeling somewhat aligned with this man who seems to be struggling as a father, Joe forms a bold theory about Scott’s whereabouts. But his covert search goes sideways, stranding Joe and Christopher in a perilous predicament deep in the Northumbrian moors.
With time running out and danger escalating, Rose, Joe and Raj must pool their findings to identify the burnt remains, track down the arsonist and expose the motive behind the blaze before the truth burns out completely. programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc:
With exclusive access to the police service on the paradise island of Bermuda, we follow life on the front line for the near 400 officers keeping both holidaymakers and locals safe. From patrols and traffic operations to the drug unit, forensics, tactical response teams, the coastguard and community policing, the series goes behind the scenes with the officers at the heart of the action.
The island has its fair share of challenges on both land and sea, with more than 3,000 crimes committed each year. We show how these dedicated officers, including around 30 from the UK, deal with the highs and lows of policing this British Overseas Territory.
In the centre of the island, Sergeant Milton Hill responds to reports of an elderly man walking along a busy roadside in clear distress. When he arrives, the man is unable to recall his name, address or basic personal details, and the mystery begins. Concerned for his safety, Milton stays close, guiding traffic around him as he repeatedly steps into the road. On an island where everyone knows everyone, Officer Milton sends a photograph of the man to base, where his identity provides a surprising twist to the tale. It's a race against time for Officer Milton to get him returned home safely.
Elsewhere, PC Eddie Smith and PC Jameela Sabir are on a stop-and-search operation. When Sergeant Mervin Homer examines a bike, he discovers a dangerous switchblade hidden under the seat. With the rider offering no feasible explanation, the prohibited weapon is immediately seized. programme.title: Celebration Kitchen
programme.desc:
Matt Tebbutt hosts this special edition celebrating Guru Nanak Gurpurab or the Birthday of Guru Nanak, the founder of the Sikh faith. Considered one of the most important Sikh holy days, it is a revered celebration in Sikhism which brings people together in devotion, reflection and unity.
Every year, the occasion is marked on the full moon day of the Kartik month, which is also known as Kartik Purnima, and falls on Tuesday 24 November this year. Three exceptional cooks join Matt in the studio to share their delicious recipes that are perfect for the celebration. Award-winning British Indian food writer, columnist and trend consultant Gurdeep Loyal prepares extra-crispy potato and chickpea tikkis with a tamarind and date chutney, which would traditionally be served as street food outside the temple. Food writer, restaurateur and chef-owner of Jikoni, Ravinder Bhogal, prepares a decadent, celebratory vegetarian platter, and as no feast is complete without a sweet treat, Manpreet Singh Ahuja, aka the Singing Chef, serves up a trio of delicious sweets, including the pinnis that he remembers his mother and grandmother making for Guru Nanak Ji's birthday.
Celebrity guests include doctor and BAFTA award-winning TV presenter Dr Ranj Singh, journalist, broadcaster and best-selling author Sathnam Sanghera and journalist, broadcaster and Good Morning Britain host Ranvir Singh, who shares her cherished Guru Nanak Gurpurab traditions, memories and food favourites from the celebration. The programme also features highlights from the BBC archives. It is a show filled with fun, food and fascinating insights into one of the most important days in the Sikh calendar. Sean Fletcher is in Liverpool to meet celebrated screenwriter, author and former Children’s Laureate Frank Cottrell-Boyce, who chooses his favourite hymns and reflects on life, faith and the value of wonder.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The oceans have seasons just as the land does. Stretching across the temperate bands located between the freezing poles and the warm tropics lie the seasonal seas. Life is tough in these constantly changing waters, but if animals can persevere and adapt to change, there are myriad opportunities to not only survive but thrive here.
Winter in the seasonal seas is a battlefield. Storms whip up immense waves that can travel for thousands of miles, building to 30 metres in height before making landfall. On the Pacific coast of South America, such waves impact the lives of South America sea lions that have lived on this exposed coast for generations. Newborn pups and mothers are restricted to the colony, but the most intrepid males take a risk, leaving the tempestuous coast for unfamiliar waters and unusual prey - black-necked swans.
Some choose to escape, whilst others are undeterred by winters icy grip on the seasonal seas. In Patagonia, a female southern right whale arrives in the protected bay where she was likely born, in search of a mate. Testing prospective partners before accepting the best mate, she is rewarded with a gentle belly rub and embrace - a valuable pairing given that these animals were hunted to near extinction in the last century. The whaling ban increased this population from just 300 to 25,000, with a surprising twist – white calves.
As daylight lengthens and spring approaches, the greening of the seasonal seas commences. Plankton multiplies, creating huge blooms and feeding many species, including a rather peculiar crustacean, a porcelain crab. In the waters off Chile, over 200 million feast on this bounty, forming the largest-known aggregation of crabs in our oceans. But with limited space and an increased flow of plankton, the crabs do something remarkable - they organise themselves into structured lines, a behaviour that has never been filmed before.
As forests flourish on land, they also do so in the water. In spring, kelp, one of the fastest-growing organisms on earth, can lengthen by half a metre a day, forming submarine jungles that are home to a variety of creatures. In Japan, these lush fronds conceal a rarely seen fish, an eelpout, with a length of just ten centimetres.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
In the frozen waters of the Arctic, a bowhead whale breaks the sea ice with its skull to breathe - completely at home in this seemingly hostile sea. Polar waters may seem remote, but their influence supports more than the wildlife that thrives there by helping to power a global system of ocean currents that creates extraordinary opportunities for wildlife far beyond the ice.
In the Falkland Islands, nutrient-rich water flowing north from Antarctica sustains a colony of king penguins. But returning parents weighed down with food for their chicks must try to cross a beach patrolled by an extraordinary southern sea lion, the only one known to regularly hunt king penguins on land.
Cold water from the Arctic also travels thousands of miles. In the Pacific, it cools the coast of Japan, where a male dwarf lumpsucker, about the size of a pea, must find a nest and persuade a female to enter. Once she has laid her eggs, he becomes a devoted single father, guarding them from hungry predators for 40 days and nights.
Around Antarctica, hundreds of fin whales converge on one of the greatest feeding grounds on earth. They work together in a spectacular synchronised formation, turning clockwise before lunging onto their sides to feast on Antarctic krill. Beneath the continent’s sea ice lies a remarkable world where giant sea spiders clamber over ancient glass sponges and a tiny amphipod escapes hungry icefish by hitching a ride on sea angels and venomous jellyfish.
The influence of the polar waters is so strong that it helps power global currents that cross entire oceans and circle the planet. In the North Atlantic, the Gulf Stream brings warm water from the Caribbean to the shores of Britain, attracting Atlantic bluefin tuna to hunt off the Cornish coast. These powerful predators, which can attack at 45 miles per hour, have only recently returned to British shores following international action to protect them.
But the currents all these animals rely on are changing. With a loss of sea ice, many are now weakening, driving animals to adapt – sometimes in surprising ways. Around Newfoundland, green sea urchins are losing the kelp forests that once protected them from the sun’s ultraviolet rays.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc:
Danny Sebastian visits a family business famous for its caricatures of Welsh rugby players that’s become an institution in south Wales. Former civil servant John Hughes began making Groggs in the 1960s using grog clay, hand-crafting charismatic miniatures of 1970s Welsh rugby players. In the decades since, his son Richard has expanded the range and refined the process, making Groggs highly sought-after; so much so that one west Wales collector has more than 150 of them.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
The final week of heats continues as another group of ambitious professional chefs steps up to prove they have the talent and technique to progress in the competition. But before they can look ahead, they must navigate two demanding challenges that will put their culinary skills and composure to the test.
First, it’s the skills test, where the chefs must fillet a sea bream and use it to create a shellfish risotto, finished with a spinach garnish. It’s a deceptively demanding dish, requiring sharp filleting skills to prepare the fish cleanly, precise timing to achieve perfectly cooked rice and the finesse to build a rich, balanced risotto without losing the delicate flavours of the seafood. Every element must come together seamlessly, with no room to hide behind elaborate presentation.
For some, the combination of intricate preparation and exacting technique proves daunting, leaving them struggling to keep pace. Others take the challenge in their stride, showing the confidence and control of seasoned professionals. Will the chefs’ efforts impress the judges, or will their shortcomings leave Marcus and Monica questioning whether they have what it takes to make it to the next stage?
With the skills test behind them, the chefs have the chance to show Marcus and Monica what they can do when given the freedom to cook their own food. In the signature dish round, they have 90 minutes to create a plate that reflects their personality, showcases their strengths and makes a compelling case for why they deserve to progress.
For some, it’s an opportunity to demonstrate real ambition and push their cooking in exciting new directions. For others, finding the right balance between ambition and execution proves more difficult.
The judges must decide whose cooking has made a strong enough impression to keep them in the running and whose journey ends here. programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.sub-title: Glasgow - A Fix at the Top of the Cathedral ║ S1
programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Dom and Lucia are in Scotland’s biggest city for one of their biggest, or at least highest, fixes yet. Roof works mean once-in-a-generation access to Glasgow Cathedral’s weathervane, so the pair are helping blacksmith Stacey and apprentice Jameel clean and re-gild this iconic cockerel. The medieval building has a storied history, but it definitely predates lifts, so Lucia volunteers to go boldly where no Repair Shop expert has gone before – straight to the top of the 225-foot-high spire.
Back on solid ground, Kaming, a member of Glasgow’s Hakka Chinese community, has a Chinese unicorn head he hopes Lucia can bring back to life. The fragile bamboo-and-paper mask plays an important part in celebrations and festivities, but years of vigorous dancing have left it tattered and torn, its once-proud horn now held on with sticky tape. As he is the last person, as far as he is aware, who still knows how to do the traditional dance associated with the mask, he hopes having the costume repaired will mean he’s able to teach it to future generations before it's lost forever. It’s not a simple fix though, as Lucia has to contend with unfamiliar materials and balance her artistic restoration with creating a mask that will stand up structurally to years' more use in the future.
As they travel the country, the Repair Shop experts love to meet fellow craftspeople, but it’s not all stonemasonry and pottery. There’s been a vibrant graffiti scene in Glasgow for decades, and Dom is meeting celebrated street artist Pizzaboy to discover how his large-scale works engage with the local community. programme.desc:
Five chefs remain in the race for a spot in the quarter-final, but first they must impress in two more challenges designed to test their creativity, precision and technical ability.
Marcus and Monica are joined by acclaimed South African chef Ash Valenzuela-Heeger, winner of the prestigious 2025 Michelin Young Chef Award. Her impressive career has seen her hone her craft at some of the world’s most celebrated restaurants, including London’s three-Michelin-starred Ledbury and Cape Town’s renowned Test Kitchen. She has since made her mark with Riverine Rabbit in Birmingham, which earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025.
Known for her bold, inventive cooking, Ash draws on her South African heritage and international influences, with live-fire techniques at the heart of her culinary style. She challenges the chefs to cook BBQ beef sirloin, served with BBQ maitake mushrooms, caramelised roscoff onions and a cafe au lait sauce. It’s a brief that demands a sophisticated understanding of flavour, smoke and fire, and the ability to make every element work in harmony.
With the standard rising and a quarter-final place within reach, can the contestants deliver a plate worthy of this award-winning chef’s exacting standards?
The signature dessert round is the final hurdle, and the chefs must show that they have the range and imagination to compete with the very best. This is their chance to take risks, bring their own ideas to the plate and prove that they can deliver something truly memorable. But sweet cooking demands a different kind of judgement; flavours must work in harmony, textures need to complement one another, and the finishing touches can make all the difference between a good dessert and a great one.
Marcus and Monica have seen what the chefs can do with savoury ingredients, but now they must decide who has the finesse and creative flair to progress to the next stage of the competition. programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
It’s the last quarter-final of the series, and with a place in knockout week at stake, there’s everything to play for. Four chefs return to the kitchen knowing that one false move could bring their ambitions to an abrupt end. Marcus and Monica are looking for the consistency, ingenuity and confidence that mark out a truly exceptional chef.
First up is the invention test, and the secret ingredient has a history stretching back more than 2,000 years: miso. A staple of Japanese cuisine, this fermented paste brings extraordinary depth, savoury complexity and umami to a dish. With different varieties offering their own distinctive flavours, the chefs must work out how best to make miso the star of the plate. Who will turn this humble ingredient into something exceptional, and who will fall short of expectations?
Then they face one last chance to prove they have what it takes to go all the way.
Three highly respected food writers and critics, Tom Parker Bowles, Leyla Kazim and Jimi Famurewa, wait to put the chefs’ cooking under the microscope. Between them, they’ve eaten at restaurants around the world and very little escapes their attention. They know what exceptional food looks, tastes and feels like, and they’ll be looking beyond technical skill to the details that separate a good meal from a truly memorable one.
The chefs must serve up a two-course menu that captures their culinary identity, showcases their abilities and gives these exacting critics something to talk about. Every choice matters, from the balance of flavours to the smallest finishing touch. Can they cook with enough originality and precision to make a lasting impression?
Back in the kitchen, Marcus and Monica face their biggest decision yet. With the quarter-finals coming to a close and only three places in knockout week up for grabs, they must consider the chefs’ performances across the challenges before deciding who has done enough to progress to the next stage. For those who fall short, there will be no second chance.
Who will take the next step towards the coveted MasterChef: The Professionals title, and whose journey ends at the final hurdle?

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When a burnt-out delivery van is discovered on a quiet rural road, Rose and Raj are met with a grim crime scene: a charred body in the passenger seat and no sign of the driver. Sifting through the ashes, they uncover a bizarre assortment of clues, including a melted key fob, rusted gardening tools and a bottle of imported Polish vodka.
Tracking down the van’s insured drivers leads them to Kelly Prudham, a tight-lipped agency cleaner, and Scott Smith, a devoted widowed father missing since the previous evening. Is Scott the vanished driver, or is he the unidentified victim in the passenger seat? Kelly claims concern for Scott’s young daughter Chloe, yet she stonewalls every question. However, Rose’s sharp eyes spot an identical bottle of Polish vodka in Kelly’s flat, indicating that Kelly may have a dangerous motive for concealing her and Scott’s recent movements.
Meanwhile, Joe can’t resist probing into the mystery. Dragging Brother Christopher along, he snoops around the crime scene and dives into Scott’s past. Relying on his sharp human intuition and feeling somewhat aligned with this man who seems to be struggling as a father, Joe forms a bold theory about Scott’s whereabouts. programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc:
With exclusive access to the police service on the paradise island of Bermuda, we follow life on the front line for the near 400 officers keeping both holidaymakers and locals safe. From patrols and traffic operations to the drug unit, forensics, tactical response teams, the coastguard and community policing, the series goes behind the scenes with the officers at the heart of the action.
The island has its fair share of challenges on both land and sea, with more than 3,000 crimes committed each year. We show how these dedicated officers, including around 30 from the UK, deal with the highs and lows of policing this British Overseas Territory.
In the centre of the island, Sergeant Milton Hill responds to reports of an elderly man walking along a busy roadside in clear distress. When he arrives, the man is unable to recall his name, address or basic personal details, and the mystery begins. Concerned for his safety, Milton stays close, guiding traffic around him as he repeatedly steps into the road. On an island where everyone knows everyone, Officer Milton sends a photograph of the man to base, where his identity provides a surprising twist to the tale. It's a race against time for Officer Milton to get him returned home safely.
Elsewhere, PC Eddie Smith and PC Jameela Sabir are on a stop-and-search operation. When Sergeant Mervin Homer examines a bike, he discovers a dangerous switchblade hidden under the seat. With the rider offering no feasible explanation, the prohibited weapon is immediately seized. Back at Hamilton Police Station, Custody Sergeant Francis Blackman reads the bike rider their rights, while Assistant Commissioner Martin Weekes examines other recently confiscated blades, including machetes and a samurai sword.
At Bermuda’s international airport, PC Paul 'Geordie' Watson supports Customs Officer Malcolm Martin and drugs dog Zorro while screening an incoming flight from Canada. After sweeping the aircraft cabin in just five minutes, Zorro indicates interest in two bags in the arrivals hall, leaving customs officers the job of discreetly monitoring the family before searching their bags and bringing them in for questioning. What will the canine team uncover next?

programme.title: Celebration Kitchen
programme.desc:
Matt Tebbutt hosts this special edition celebrating Guru Nanak Gurpurab or the Birthday of Guru Nanak, the founder of the Sikh faith. Considered one of the most important Sikh holy days, it is a revered celebration in Sikhism which brings people together in devotion, reflection and unity.
Every year, the occasion is marked on the full moon day of the Kartik month, which is also known as Kartik Purnima, and falls on Tuesday 24 November this year. Three exceptional cooks join Matt in the studio to share their delicious recipes that are perfect for the celebration. Award-winning British Indian food writer, columnist and trend consultant Gurdeep Loyal prepares extra-crispy potato and chickpea tikkis with a tamarind and date chutney, which would traditionally be served as street food outside the temple. Food writer, restaurateur and chef-owner of Jikoni, Ravinder Bhogal, prepares a decadent, celebratory vegetarian platter, and as no feast is complete without a sweet treat, Manpreet Singh Ahuja, aka the Singing Chef, serves up a trio of delicious sweets, including the pinnis that he remembers his mother and grandmother making for Guru Nanak Ji's birthday.
Celebrity guests include doctor and BAFTA award-winning TV presenter Dr Ranj Singh, journalist, broadcaster and best-selling author Sathnam Sanghera and journalist, broadcaster and Good Morning Britain host Ranvir Singh, who shares her cherished Guru Nanak Gurpurab traditions, memories and food favourites from the celebration. The programme also features highlights from the BBC archives. It is a show filled with fun, food and fascinating insights into one of the most important days in the Sikh calendar. programme.desc:
Sean Fletcher is in Liverpool to meet celebrated screenwriter, author and former Children’s Laureate Frank Cottrell-Boyce, who chooses his favourite hymns and reflects on life, faith and the value of wonder.
Sean meets Frank at Liverpool’s historic waterfront, where Frank's story began, and discovers how a childhood steeped in Catholic community and the stories of saints inspired his young imagination.
In Liverpool’s Central Library, Sean hears how Frank went on to become a screenwriter for TV and film, and a best-selling children’s author. Their journey through Liverpool finally brings them to the city’s iconic Metropolitan Cathedral, where Frank talks of the architecture as a prayer and tells of hearing his children sing there many years ago.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The oceans have seasons just as the land does. Stretching across the temperate bands located between the freezing poles and the warm tropics lie the seasonal seas. Life is tough in these constantly changing waters, but if animals can persevere and adapt to change, there are myriad opportunities to not only survive but thrive here.
Winter in the seasonal seas is a battlefield. Storms whip up immense waves that can travel for thousands of miles, building to 30 metres in height before making landfall. On the Pacific coast of South America, such waves impact the lives of South America sea lions that have lived on this exposed coast for generations. Newborn pups and mothers are restricted to the colony, but the most intrepid males take a risk, leaving the tempestuous coast for unfamiliar waters and unusual prey - black-necked swans.
Some choose to escape, whilst others are undeterred by winters icy grip on the seasonal seas. In Patagonia, a female southern right whale arrives in the protected bay where she was likely born, in search of a mate. Testing prospective partners before accepting the best mate, she is rewarded with a gentle belly rub and embrace - a valuable pairing given that these animals were hunted to near extinction in the last century. The whaling ban increased this population from just 300 to 25,000, with a surprising twist – white calves.
As daylight lengthens and spring approaches, the greening of the seasonal seas commences. Plankton multiplies, creating huge blooms and feeding many species, including a rather peculiar crustacean, a porcelain crab. In the waters off Chile, over 200 million feast on this bounty, forming the largest-known aggregation of crabs in our oceans. But with limited space and an increased flow of plankton, the crabs do something remarkable - they organise themselves into structured lines, a behaviour that has never been filmed before.
As forests flourish on land, they also do so in the water. In spring, kelp, one of the fastest-growing organisms on earth, can lengthen by half a metre a day, forming submarine jungles that are home to a variety of creatures. In Japan, these lush fronds conceal a rarely seen fish, an eelpout, with a length of just ten centimetres.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
In the frozen waters of the Arctic, a bowhead whale breaks the sea ice with its skull to breathe - completely at home in this seemingly hostile sea. Polar waters may seem remote, but their influence supports more than the wildlife that thrives there by helping to power a global system of ocean currents that creates extraordinary opportunities for wildlife far beyond the ice.
In the Falkland Islands, nutrient-rich water flowing north from Antarctica sustains a colony of king penguins. But returning parents weighed down with food for their chicks must try to cross a beach patrolled by an extraordinary southern sea lion, the only one known to regularly hunt king penguins on land.
Cold water from the Arctic also travels thousands of miles. In the Pacific, it cools the coast of Japan, where a male dwarf lumpsucker, about the size of a pea, must find a nest and persuade a female to enter. Once she has laid her eggs, he becomes a devoted single father, guarding them from hungry predators for 40 days and nights.
Around Antarctica, hundreds of fin whales converge on one of the greatest feeding grounds on earth. They work together in a spectacular synchronised formation, turning clockwise before lunging onto their sides to feast on Antarctic krill. Beneath the continent’s sea ice lies a remarkable world where giant sea spiders clamber over ancient glass sponges and a tiny amphipod escapes hungry icefish by hitching a ride on sea angels and venomous jellyfish.
The influence of the polar waters is so strong that it helps power global currents that cross entire oceans and circle the planet. In the North Atlantic, the Gulf Stream brings warm water from the Caribbean to the shores of Britain, attracting Atlantic bluefin tuna to hunt off the Cornish coast. These powerful predators, which can attack at 45 miles per hour, have only recently returned to British shores following international action to protect them.
But the currents all these animals rely on are changing. With a loss of sea ice, many are now weakening, driving animals to adapt – sometimes in surprising ways. Around Newfoundland, green sea urchins are losing the kelp forests that once protected them from the sun’s ultraviolet rays.
